components.name: uv
components._comment: Astral standalone uv installer. No committed byte digest or upstream provenance identity is available in this repository, so this stays transport_trusted (HTTPS + release-account trust only) and is NOT release-verified. Pinning requires the maintainer release script to record an exact uv version + per-artifact sha256.

artifacts.blocker: No committed sha256 for uv-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu; maintainer must run scripts/release/update_supply_chain_manifest.py.

components.name: tirith
components._comment: sheeki03/tirith security scanner. Upstream publishes a Sigstore keyless provenance identity (recorded per-artifact below) which IS an independent anchor; however the installed code still resolves 'releases/latest' with no exact version pin, so the component stays transport_trusted until an exact release is pinned. When pinned, this component becomes release_verified via provenance.

artifacts.blocker: Version is resolved as 'releases/latest' in code; pin an exact tirith release to satisfy the immutable-identity requirement.
artifacts.operator_guidance: Tirith is optional; when unpinned, Hermes falls back to pattern-matching guards. See docs/security/supply-chain-trust-root.md.

components.name: electron
components._comment: Electron runtime for the desktop app. The npm tarball (electron-41.10.3.tgz) is lock-integrity-bound (sha512) in the root package-lock.json; the per-platform binary archive is the canonical Electron release ZIP whose exact sha256 is COMMITTED below (taken from node_modules/electron/checksums.json, which electron@41.10.3 ships in its package `files` and which @electron/get verifies against the signed SHASUMS256.txt). apps/desktop/scripts/verify-native-payloads.mjs compares the package-bundled checksums.json against THIS committed digest for the exact target before any build — a mirror (ELECTRON_MIRROR) may change WHERE the archive is fetched, never the accepted digest. node-pty / get-windows native binaries are staged only from lock-bound bundled prebuilds; the network rebuild fails closed.

components.name: get-windows
components._comment: get-windows native window-detection binding for the desktop app (read_window_below). Its npm lifecycle script ('node-pre-gyp install --fallback-to-build') is DISABLED in the root package.json allowScripts allowlist, so 'npm ci' never downloads or compiles a native binary and node-pre-gyp is never spawned. The Windows N-API binding (node-get-windows.node, a PE) is downloaded by node-pre-gyp from the package's GitHub releases host as a .tar.gz; the macOS Swift helper ('main', a universal Mach-O) ships inside the lock-integrity-bound npm tarball. PROVENANCE SPLIT: each artifact 'digest' authenticates the URL BYTES (the archive: the GitHub .tar.gz for Windows, the npm .tgz for macOS whose sha512 EQUALS the root package-lock integrity for get-windows), while 'member_digests' pins the sha256 of the EXTRACTED file that is actually staged. apps/desktop/scripts/stage-native-deps.mjs verifies the MEMBER digest of the on-disk binding AND its PE/Mach-O magic before staging; a download verifier would check the archive 'digest'. A mutated/unpinned/unmarked member is REJECTED (fail closed); a target with no member digest (win32-arm64, linux) has the feature disabled with no network/build fallback.
